```{r}
# ============================================================
#  compare_clusterings.R
#  Compares two cluster assignments for the same set of items.
#  - Adjusted Rand Index (ARI)
#  - Contingency / overlap table
#  - Sankey / alluvial plot
#
#  Dependencies: fossil, ggalluvial, ggplot2, dplyr
#  Install once with:
#    install.packages(c("fossil", "ggalluvial", "ggplot2", "dplyr"))
# ============================================================

library(fossil)       # adj.rand.index
library(aricode)      # AMI (adjusted mutual information)
library(clue)         # solve_LSAP (Hungarian algorithm)
library(ggalluvial)   # alluvial / Sankey plot
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)
library(RColorBrewer)
 
# ── Colour helper: randomised palette for arbitrary n ───────
#
# Combines several RColorBrewer palettes into one large pool,
# then samples without replacement.  Works up to ~70 clusters;
# beyond that colours will start to look similar regardless of
# method — consider switching to a heatmap at that point.
make_palette <- function(n, seed = 123) {
  set.seed(seed)
  pool <- unique(c(
    RColorBrewer::brewer.pal(12, "Set3"),
    RColorBrewer::brewer.pal(8,  "Set1"),
    RColorBrewer::brewer.pal(8,  "Dark2"),
    RColorBrewer::brewer.pal(8,  "Accent"),
    RColorBrewer::brewer.pal(12, "Paired"),
    RColorBrewer::brewer.pal(11, "Spectral")
  ))
  if (n > length(pool)) {
    # Fall back to colorRampPalette if we somehow exceed the pool
    warning(sprintf(
      "Requested %d colours but pool only has %d distinct ones; some will repeat.",
      n, length(pool)
    ))
    colorRampPalette(pool)(n)
  } else {
    sample(pool, n)
  }
}
 
# ── 1. Main comparison function ─────────────────────────────
 
#' Compare two cluster assignments for the same items
#'
#' @param df1  Data frame with columns: name (item ID), cluster (group label)
#' @param df2  Data frame with columns: name (item ID), cluster (group label)
#' @param name_col    Name of the column containing item identifiers (default "name")
#' @param cluster_col Name of the column containing cluster labels  (default "cluster")
#' @param plot        Logical — produce a Sankey plot? (default TRUE)
#' @param label1      Label for df1 in the plot (default "Assignment 1")
#' @param label2      Label for df2 in the plot (default "Assignment 2")
#'
#' @return A list with: ari, ami, pct_misclassified, hungarian_mapping,
#'         contingency_table, plot (ggplot object or NULL)
compare_clusterings <- function(df1, df2,
                                name_col    = "name",
                                cluster_col = "cluster",
                                plot   = TRUE,
                                label1 = "Assignment 1",
                                label2 = "Assignment 2") {
 
  # ── Validate inputs ────────────────────────────────────────
  stopifnot(
    is.data.frame(df1), is.data.frame(df2),
    name_col    %in% names(df1), name_col    %in% names(df2),
    cluster_col %in% names(df1), cluster_col %in% names(df2)
  )
 
  # Rename for convenience
  df1 <- df1[, c(name_col, cluster_col)]
  df2 <- df2[, c(name_col, cluster_col)]
  names(df1) <- c("name", "cluster")
  names(df2) <- c("name", "cluster")
 
  # ── Align on shared items ───────────────────────────────────
  merged <- inner_join(df1, df2, by = "name", suffix = c("_1", "_2"))
 
  n_df1  <- nrow(df1)
  n_df2  <- nrow(df2)
  n_shared <- nrow(merged)
 
  if (n_shared == 0) stop("No items in common between the two data frames.")
  if (n_shared < n_df1 | n_shared < n_df2) {
    message(sprintf(
      "Note: %d item(s) not shared between data frames and were excluded.",
      max(n_df1, n_df2) - n_shared
    ))
  }
 
  # ── Adjusted Rand Index ─────────────────────────────────────
  # adj.rand.index requires integer or numeric vectors
  c1_int <- as.integer(factor(merged$cluster_1))
  c2_int <- as.integer(factor(merged$cluster_2))
 
  ari <- adj.rand.index(c1_int, c2_int)
 
  # ── Adjusted Mutual Information (arithmetic normalisation) ──
  ami <- AMI(merged$cluster_1, merged$cluster_2)
 
  # ── % Misclassified via Hungarian algorithm ─────────────────
  #
  # Build a cost matrix (mismatches) between df1 and df2 cluster labels,
  # then find the optimal 1-to-1 assignment that minimises total cost.
  #
  # Note: Hungarian requires a square matrix, so we pad with dummy rows/cols
  # if the two sides have different numbers of clusters. Items assigned to
  # unmatched clusters (from the smaller side) are counted as misclassified.
 
  lvl1 <- levels(factor(merged$cluster_1))
  lvl2 <- levels(factor(merged$cluster_2))
  k    <- max(length(lvl1), length(lvl2))
 
  # Overlap count matrix (rows = df1 clusters, cols = df2 clusters)
  overlap_mat <- matrix(0L, nrow = k, ncol = k)
  for (i in seq_along(lvl1)) {
    for (j in seq_along(lvl2)) {
      overlap_mat[i, j] <- sum(merged$cluster_1 == lvl1[i] &
                               merged$cluster_2 == lvl2[j])
    }
  }
 
  # Hungarian: maximise overlap  ↔  minimise (max - overlap)
  cost_mat    <- max(overlap_mat) - overlap_mat
  assignment  <- clue::solve_LSAP(cost_mat)   # assignment[i] = best df2 col for df1 row i
 
  # Build readable mapping table (only for real, non-padded clusters)
  hungarian_mapping <- data.frame(
    df1_cluster = lvl1,
    df2_cluster = ifelse(assignment[seq_along(lvl1)] <= length(lvl2),
                         lvl2[assignment[seq_along(lvl1)]],
                         NA_character_)
  )
 
  # Count correctly classified items
  n_correct <- sum(mapply(function(c1, c2) {
    matched_c2 <- hungarian_mapping$df2_cluster[hungarian_mapping$df1_cluster == c1]
    length(matched_c2) > 0 && !is.na(matched_c2) && c2 == matched_c2
  }, merged$cluster_1, merged$cluster_2))
 
  pct_misclassified <- 100 * (1 - n_correct / n_shared)
 
  # ── Console summary ─────────────────────────────────────────
  cat("─────────────────────────────────────────\n")
  cat(sprintf(" Adjusted Rand Index (ARI):        %.4f\n", ari))
  cat(" (1 = perfect agreement, ~0 = random)\n\n")
  cat(sprintf(" Adjusted Mutual Information (AMI): %.4f\n", ami))
  cat(" (1 = perfect agreement, ~0 = random)\n\n")
  cat(sprintf(" %% Misclassified (Hungarian):       %.2f%%\n", pct_misclassified))
  cat(sprintf(" (%d of %d items do not fall in their optimally matched cluster)\n",
              n_shared - n_correct, n_shared))
  if (length(lvl1) != length(lvl2)) {
    cat(sprintf(
      " Warning: unequal cluster counts (%d vs %d) — %d cluster(s) left unmatched.\n",
      length(lvl1), length(lvl2), abs(length(lvl1) - length(lvl2))
    ))
  }
  cat("─────────────────────────────────────────\n\n")
 
  cat("Optimal cluster mapping (Hungarian):\n")
  print(hungarian_mapping)
  cat("\n")
 
  # ── Contingency table ───────────────────────────────────────
  # Sort factor levels numerically where possible, for readable row/col order
  sort_num_or_chr <- function(x) {
    u    <- unique(as.character(x))
    nums <- suppressWarnings(as.numeric(u))
    if (all(!is.na(nums))) factor(x, levels = u[order(nums)])
    else                   factor(x)
  }
 
  cont <- table(
    df1_cluster = sort_num_or_chr(merged$cluster_1),
    df2_cluster = sort_num_or_chr(merged$cluster_2)
  )
 
  cat("Overlap / contingency table (counts):\n")
  print(cont)
  cat("\nRow proportions (fraction of each df1 cluster in each df2 cluster):\n")
  print(round(prop.table(cont, margin = 1), 3))
  cat("\n")
 
  # ── Sankey / alluvial plot ──────────────────────────────────
  p <- NULL
  if (plot) {
 
    # Helper: sort cluster labels numerically if all values are numeric,
    # otherwise fall back to standard alphabetical order
    sorted_levels <- function(x) {
      u <- unique(as.character(x))
      nums <- suppressWarnings(as.numeric(u))
      if (all(!is.na(nums))) u[order(nums)] else sort(u)
    }
 
    ord1 <- sorted_levels(merged$cluster_1)
    ord2 <- sorted_levels(merged$cluster_2)
 
    # Build frequency table; keep cluster columns as plain character so we
    # can set factor levels ourselves for correct axis ordering
    alluvial_df <- merged %>%
      count(cluster_1, cluster_2) %>%
      mutate(
        cluster_1 = factor(as.character(cluster_1), levels = ord1),
        cluster_2 = factor(as.character(cluster_2), levels = ord2)
      )
 
    pal <- make_palette(length(ord1))
    names(pal) <- ord1
 
    # ── Compute stratum midpoints for leader lines ──────────────
    #
    # ggalluvial stacks strata top-to-bottom in factor-level order,
    # so the first level is at the TOP and y accumulates downward.
    # We reverse the level order for cumsum, then flip back.
    #
    # axis1 (df1) strata
    totals1 <- alluvial_df %>%
      group_by(cluster_1) %>%
      summarise(total = sum(n), .groups = "drop") %>%
      arrange(match(cluster_1, rev(ord1))) %>%   # top level first = last in ord1
      mutate(
        ymax = cumsum(total),
        ymid = ymax - total / 2
      )
 
    # axis2 (df2) strata
    totals2 <- alluvial_df %>%
      group_by(cluster_2) %>%
      summarise(total = sum(n), .groups = "drop") %>%
      arrange(match(cluster_2, rev(ord2))) %>%
      mutate(
        ymax = cumsum(total),
        ymid = ymax - total / 2
      )
 
    # Leader line geometry (in ggalluvial's internal x-scale):
    #   axis1 is at x = 1, axis2 is at x = 2
    #   stratum half-width = 0.3 / 2 = 0.15
    #   elbow x: step out 0.12 beyond the stratum edge
    #   text x:  a further 0.08 beyond the elbow
    x1_edge  <- 1 - 0.15          # left  edge of axis1 strata
    x2_edge  <- 2 + 0.15          # right edge of axis2 strata
    x1_elbow <- x1_edge - 0.12
    x2_elbow <- x2_edge + 0.12
    x1_text  <- x1_elbow - 0.08
    x2_text  <- x2_elbow + 0.08
 
    leaders1 <- totals1 %>%
      mutate(
        x_start = x1_edge,
        x_elbow = x1_elbow,
        x_text  = x1_text,
        label   = as.character(cluster_1)
      )
 
    leaders2 <- totals2 %>%
      mutate(
        x_start = x2_edge,
        x_elbow = x2_elbow,
        x_text  = x2_text,
        label   = as.character(cluster_2)
      )
 
    # y-positions for the horizontal baseline: evenly spaced across the full
    # y range so labels never overlap regardless of cluster size
    y_total <- sum(totals1$total)
    n1 <- nrow(leaders1)
    n2 <- nrow(leaders2)
 
    # Even spacing top-to-bottom: arrange by ymid descending so label order
    # follows strata order visually
    leaders1 <- leaders1 %>%
      arrange(desc(ymid)) %>%
      mutate(y_text = seq(y_total, 0, length.out = n1 + 2)[seq(2, n1 + 1)])
 
    leaders2 <- leaders2 %>%
      arrange(desc(ymid)) %>%
      mutate(y_text = seq(y_total, 0, length.out = n2 + 2)[seq(2, n2 + 1)])
 
    # Expand plot limits to make room for leader lines
    x_expand <- 0.55
 
    p <- ggplot(alluvial_df,
                aes(axis1 = cluster_1, axis2 = cluster_2, y = n)) +
      geom_alluvium(aes(fill = cluster_1), alpha = 0.75, width = 0.3) +
      geom_stratum(width = 0.3, fill = "grey92", colour = "grey40") +
      # Angled segment: stratum midpoint → elbow (at label y)
      geom_segment(
        data = leaders1,
        aes(x = x_start, xend = x_elbow, y = ymid, yend = y_text),
        colour = "grey50", linewidth = 0.3, inherit.aes = FALSE
      ) +
      # Horizontal segment: elbow → text anchor
      geom_segment(
        data = leaders1,
        aes(x = x_elbow, xend = x_text, y = y_text, yend = y_text),
        colour = "grey50", linewidth = 0.3, inherit.aes = FALSE
      ) +
      geom_text(
        data = leaders1,
        aes(x = x_text, y = y_text, label = label),
        hjust = 1, size = 4.2, inherit.aes = FALSE
      ) +
      geom_segment(
        data = leaders2,
        aes(x = x_start, xend = x_elbow, y = ymid, yend = y_text),
        colour = "grey50", linewidth = 0.3, inherit.aes = FALSE
      ) +
      geom_segment(
        data = leaders2,
        aes(x = x_elbow, xend = x_text, y = y_text, yend = y_text),
        colour = "grey50", linewidth = 0.3, inherit.aes = FALSE
      ) +
      geom_text(
        data = leaders2,
        aes(x = x_text, y = y_text, label = label),
        hjust = 0, size = 4.2, inherit.aes = FALSE
      ) +
      scale_x_continuous(
        breaks = c(1, 2),
        labels = c(label1, label2),
        limits = c(1 - x_expand, 2 + x_expand)
      ) +
      scale_fill_manual(values = pal, guide = "none") +
      labs(
        title    = "Cluster assignment comparison",
        subtitle = sprintf("ARI = %.4f  |  AMI = %.4f  |  %.1f%% disagreement  |  n = %d items",
                           ari, ami, pct_misclassified, n_shared),
        y = "Number of items",
        x = NULL
      ) +
      theme_minimal(base_size = 13) +
      theme(
        panel.grid  = element_blank(),
        axis.text.x = element_text(face = "bold", size = 12)
      )
 
    print(p)
  }
 
  # ── Return results invisibly ────────────────────────────────
  invisible(list(
    ari               = ari,
    ami               = ami,
    pct_misclassified = pct_misclassified,
    hungarian_mapping = hungarian_mapping,
    n_items           = n_shared,
    contingency_table = cont,
    plot              = p
  ))
}




# Run the comparison
result <- compare_clusterings(
  Mass_PopPUNK_local, Mass_GPSCs,
  name_col    = "Taxon",
  cluster_col = "Cluster",
  label1      = "Local PopPUNK clusters",
  label2      = "GPSCs"
)

result <- compare_clusterings(
  Mass_GPSCs, Mass_PopPUNK_local,
  name_col    = "Taxon",
  cluster_col = "Cluster",
  label2      = "Local PopPUNK clusters",
  label1      = "GPSCs"
)

# Access individual outputs:
# result$ari
# result$ami
# result$pct_misclassified
# result$hungarian_mapping   # data frame: df1 cluster → best-matched df2 cluster
# result$contingency_table
# result$plot
```
